subtopics.title: What a Contour Line Actually Is

questions.question: A contour line joins all points that:
options: Are the same height above sea level
Lie the same distance from the river

questions.question: On our map the contour interval is 20 m. A point lies between the 820 m and 840 m contour lines. Its height is:
Why can two contour lines never cross each other?
options: It would make the map untidy
Rivers would have nowhere to flow
A single point cannot have two different heights at once

questions.question: What extra information does a spot height of 913 give that contours cannot?
options: The exact altitude of the summit, not just 'above the highest contour'
The depth of the nearest river

subtopics.title: Spacing Is Gradient — Steep and Gentle Slopes

questions.question: WHY does close spacing mean a steep slope?
options: Because more lines mean more height in total
Because the fixed 20 m rise happens over a shorter horizontal distance
Because steep land erodes contour lines closer
Because mapmakers draw steep areas darker

questions.question: Contours widely spaced at the TOP of a slope and tightly packed at the BOTTOM indicate:
options: A convex slope — gentle at the top, steepening below, with a blind spot from the summit

questions.question: On which slope can a person standing at the summit see the entire slope down to its foot?
options: A concave slope — steep at the top, easing towards the bottom

questions.question: The best exam justification for 'this is the steepest slope' is:
options: 'The contour lines are closest together here, so the land rises 20 m over the shortest horizontal distance'

subtopics.title: Finding the River Valley — the V Rule

questions.question: In a river valley, the V-shaped bends in the contour lines point:
options: Downhill, in the direction of flow
Uphill, toward the higher ground upstream

questions.question: The contours crossing a river read 840, 820, 800 in the direction you trace it. The river is flowing:
options: In the direction you are tracing — heights must decrease downstream
Against the direction you are tracing

questions.question: How do you tell a spur from a valley on a contour map?
options: A spur has closer contours than a valley
A spur's contours bulge downhill away from the summit and never carry a river; a valley's V points uphill and often holds a river

subtopics.title: Reading the Whole Landscape — and the Exam Method

questions.question: Closed, roughly circular contours with values rising toward the centre represent:
Contour lines so close together they almost touch indicate:
What is the FIRST step of the five-step exam method for any contour question?
options: Read the contour interval from the map key

questions.question: A strong mapwork answer always:
options: Names the feature, quotes the contour evidence, and reads the heights
Copies the map key word for word

subtopics.title: Walking the Hill — What the Lines Really Are

questions.question: Walking along a footpath that follows a contour line, you would:
options: Stay at exactly the same height the whole way

questions.question: On this map, the height difference between one contour line and the next is:
Why can a contour line never simply stop in the middle of the map?
options: A level path around a hill must return to where it started, or run off the edge of the sheet
It can stop, at a cliff

questions.question: The rings tell you the summit is above 900 m; the dot marked 913 tells you:
options: The height of the nearest town
The exact height of that one spot — 913 metres
How many contour lines there are

questions.question: In the shopping-centre comparison, contour lines spread far apart are like:
Two contour lines look as if they are touching. This means:
options: The map has a printing mistake
A cliff — 20 m of height gained with almost no horizontal distance

questions.question: You leave the summit on sharply falling ground and it flattens out towards the bottom. The contour lines are:
options: Crowded near the top and spread out lower down — a concave slope
Spread out near the top and crowded near the bottom

questions.question: Why can you not see the foot of a convex slope from its summit?
options: The bulge of the gentler upper slope hides the steeper ground below
Because the contour lines are too close

subtopics.title: Finding the River Without Looking for Blue

questions.question: A contour line meeting a valley detours up the valley and back out again because:
options: It must stay at the same height, and the valley floor is lower
It is avoiding the spot height

questions.question: The pointed end of the V in a valley's contours points towards:
options: The high ground the stream comes from
The lowest point on the map

questions.question: A bend in the contours points AWAY from the higher numbers. The feature is:
What is the most reliable way to settle whether a bend is a valley or a spur?
options: Read the contour values on either side to find which way is uphill
Guess from the shape of the bend
Check whether the bend is drawn in bold
Measure the length of the bend
